lessons: ROOT CAUSE 1 (drift): this skill's central fact had an expiry date and nothing watched it. v1.2.2 correctly recorded that Directive 364 would take effect on 18/05/2026 and repeal 357/361/363, then went on describing 361 as operative. The information was IN the skill and in its own evidence.json; what was missing was any step comparing a stated future effective date against today. Every future-dated commencement in evidence.json is a diary entry, not a fact to restate.

ROOT CAUSE 2 (scope), and the more serious of the two: the skill applied Bank of Israel banking directives to INSURERS for its entire life, and routed non-bank payment providers to BOI when the Payment Services Law vests that in the Israel Securities Authority. The drift fix did not surface either, because every check asked 'is this instrument in force?' and none asked 'whom does this instrument bind?'. Directive 364's applicability clause settles it in one sentence and the word 'ביטוח' appears nowhere in its 57 pages. **Add the addressee question as question 0 of the standing check.** A skill can be perfectly current and still send half its users to the wrong regulator.

The evidence gate extracted 0 facts and 6 URLs before the edit and cannot see directive numbers, statute names or dates, which is this skill's entire factual content. It exited 0 on a skill whose headline claim was three months stale AND whose scope was wrong. After adding regulation and section citations it extracts real facts. On regulatory skills a green evidence gate is evidence of nothing.

The skill had NO domain-checklist.md, so the Expert gate had nothing to anchor against. One was written this cycle, and its first draft still had the blind spot in ROOT CAUSE 2: every Must-cover row was an instrument-status question and none was a scope question.

Cleanup was incomplete twice, and both times an independent reviewer caught it rather than a grep of mine. Corrections landed in the prose and headline sections but not in bullet lists, reference files and metadata.json. After correcting a claim, grep the whole skill folder for the CLAIM'S SUBJECT (cloud approval, reporting clock, pre-launch submission), not just the old wording, and check metadata.json, which no gate reads.

Fabricated quantities recur in this domain and all have the shape of real rules: ISA thresholds of 24 hours and 1% of equity, a four-tier INCD deadline ladder, a 48-hour patch SLA, quarterly board reporting, an annual pen test by a 'certified' firm. The 24h/72h pair appears to be the PENDING bill's clocks back-dated onto present obligations. If a skill states a number a regulator would have to publish, find the publication or delete the number.

A reviewer flagged the cloud pre-approval claim as UNVERIFIED rather than wrong; reading Directive 362's PDF showed it was wrong three ways at once (repealed directive cited, wrong mechanism, and the regulator's stated posture is the opposite: 'Business enabler'). An UNVERIFIED flag on something the skill states as a hard requirement deserves the same primary-source read as a claim asserted to be false.

I wrote a sentence into the skill claiming an exact-phrase search of the ISA corpus returned zero results. I had not run that search; a subagent had. Narrowed to what I personally verified (105-33 read in full, contains no percentage). Do not restate a subagent's method as your own finding.

boi.org.il sits behind Radware and returns ~108 characters to curl and WebFetch, which a status-code check reads as HTTP 200. One such body contained the substring '361' inside an incident ID, which a careless grep would score as a content match.

[CARRY] Map the control matrix to Directive 364's actual clause numbers. The 57-page PDF is at boi.org.il/media/zsznzgay/364.pdf and was read this cycle only for the applicability and board-cadence clauses.
[CARRY] Supply-chain cyber, the whole of absorbed Directive 363, still gets two lines. It is the highest-frequency real incident vector for Israeli banks.

[CARRY] Watch for enactment of the National Cyber Defense Law (bill 1955, committee stage on 29/07/2026). On enactment: statutory clocks, essential-organisation designation, mandatory CISO, four-route standards menu.

[CARRY] Expert MAJORs deferred: dual-listed issuers and foreign entities with Israeli operations have no lane; cloud outside banking is uncovered; the one-event-three-reporting-lines sequence is stated as a principle but never assembled into an ordered playbook; director and officer personal liability is absent; non-bank credit providers and currency service providers are missing from the framework map.

[CARRY] Directives 362, 366 and 367 were all updated on 17/06/2026. Check that cluster as a group next cycle, and add 369 (model risk management) which is increasingly relevant as banks put AI into fraud pipelines.
